crimea_ukraine.note: Russia annexed Crimea in March 2014 after a referendum the UN declared invalid; UN General Assembly Resolution 68/262 (27 March 2014) affirmed Ukraine's internationally recognized borders, and non-recognition of the annexation remains the prevailing position.
crimea_ukraine.policy: Render Crimea as internationally recognized Ukrainian territory under Russian de facto occupation, noting the occupation as metadata rather than a sovereignty transfer.

default_policy.note: Renders the de facto controlled boundary by default and carries de jure claim lines and point-of-view variants as separate metadata layers, consistent with Natural Earth's disputed-boundaries convention and the UN member-state list (193 members + 2 observer states).
default_policy.policy: Internationally recognized borders by default; disputed control shown as metadata where available, not silently resolved.

_borders.description: How the map renders sovereign borders and handles disputed sovereignty.

israel_palestine.note: Palestine has been a UN non-member observer state since November 2012 (rights expanded by Resolution ES-10/23 in May 2024); as of September 2025 it is recognized by about 157 of 193 UN members, including a 2025 wave of recognitions led by France, Canada, and the UK.
israel_palestine.policy: Show Israel as a recognized sovereign state and the State of Palestine (West Bank including East Jerusalem, and Gaza) as a partially recognized UN non-member observer state, with borders, settlements, and East Jerusalem's status carried as disputed metadata.

kosovo.note: As of late 2025 roughly 110 of 193 UN members recognize Kosovo (Belgrade cites a lower figure after withdrawals); Kosovo is not a UN member, and 5 EU states plus Serbia withhold recognition. It has no official ISO 3166-1 code and uses the placeholder XK.
kosovo.policy: Treat Kosovo as a partially recognized de facto state (independence declared 2008), explicitly flagging that recognition is contested and Serbia does not recognize it.

_borders.label: Borders & territory provenance

taiwan.note: The PRC holds the China seat at the UN (GA Resolution 2758, 1971) and Taiwan is not a UN member; ISO 3166 lists it as 'Taiwan, Province of China' (TW). As of 2025 the ROC retains formal diplomatic relations with about 12 states.
taiwan.policy: Show Taiwan (Republic of China) as a de facto self-governing entity with its own ISO 3166-1 code (TW), flagging the PRC's claim and Taiwan's lack of a UN seat as metadata.

western_sahara.note: A UN Non-Self-Governing Territory since 1963 with self-determination still pending; MINURSO's mandate was renewed on 31 October 2025, and a US-sponsored Security Council resolution that month endorsed Morocco's autonomy plan as a basis for negotiations, while Polisario (backed by Algeria) continues to demand a referendum.
western_sahara.policy: Mark Western Sahara as a UN-listed Non-Self-Governing Territory with no internationally recognized sovereign, showing Moroccan de facto control and SADR/Polisario control as disputed metadata rather than settled sovereignty.

additionalSources.datasetTitle: Data Book 2023 and 2024 (Geographical Distribution of Operations)
Statistics on International Development: Final UK ODA Spend 2024
PLF 2025 budget review, citing DG Tresor / OECD bilateral ODA data (2022)
Money Matters: How is Germany spending its aid? (2024 data)

aid.colorMeaning: Path color/weight encodes the estimated annual bilateral aid amount from donor to recipient.
aid.label: Foreign aid flows
aid.limitations: Donors use different definitions and instruments (grants vs. loan commitments vs. total assistance), so figures are not on a single harmonized basis - see each corridor's tooltip for its specific source and definition. Deliberately excludes corridors where aid is overwhelmingly military/security in nature (US to Ukraine and US to Israel are both majority security-classified) since including them at full value alongside development-focused corridors would misrepresent the comparison. This is a sample of major corridors from five donors, not an exhaustive bilateral matrix.
aid.methodology: Each corridor uses the donor's own official aid reporting for the most recent available year (2022-2024, varies by donor). US figures combine each country's total obligation with its officially-stated economic-assistance share; Japan figures are JICA ODA-loan and investment-finance commitments (a specific instrument, not total bilateral ODA); UK and France figures are each government's bilateral ODA disbursements, converted to USD at that year's average exchange rate.
aid.metric: Bilateral foreign aid / official development assistance from major donor governments to recipient countries.

primarySource.datasetTitle: US Foreign Aid by Country (ForeignAssistance.gov data)

aid.unit: USD millions/year (donor definitions vary - see limitations)

additionalSources.datasetTitle: Annual Report 2024 / small arms trade updates

arms.colorMeaning: Path color/weight encodes the volume or value of arms transferred along supplier–recipient corridors.
arms.label: Arms trafficking
arms.limitations: SIPRI covers legal major-arms transfers only (real flow pairs), while illicit small-arms corridors are estimated and partial because diversion is by definition under-reported.
arms.methodology: SIPRI tracks deliveries of major conventional arms by supplier/recipient as trend-indicator values; Small Arms Survey models authorized small-arms trade and overlays illicit-diversion research.
arms.metric: Transfers of conventional arms and small arms between supplier and recipient countries, including illicit diversion.

primarySource.datasetTitle: Arms Transfers Database / Trends in International Arms Transfers 2025

additionalSources.datasetTitle: Health Workforce Support and Safeguards List 2023 / Global Code of Practice on International Recruitment

braindrain.colorMeaning: Path color/weight encodes the volume of health professionals trained in an origin country and working abroad.
braindrain.label: Medical brain drain
braindrain.limitations: Coverage is destination = OECD only (South-South flows missing), measures stock of professionals present rather than recruitment flow, and corridors drawn between centroids are indicative.
braindrain.methodology: Counts foreign-trained doctors and nurses in OECD destination countries by country of training, from national registers and censuses.
braindrain.metric: Origin-to-destination movement of foreign-trained doctors and nurses working in destination (mainly OECD) countries.

primarySource.datasetTitle: International Migration Outlook 2025 — International migration of health professionals to OECD countries

cables.colorMeaning: Lines depict individual submarine cable systems (color distinguishes systems, not magnitude).
cables.label: Submarine cables
cables.limitations: Routes are schematic/stylized representations, not exact geodetic cable paths, and the free dataset lacks precise geocoded geometry.
cables.methodology: Cable systems, landing stations, ownership, length, and service dates compiled from operator filings and industry research.
cables.metric: Routes of submarine communications cable systems and their landing points.

primarySource.datasetTitle: Submarine Cable Map

additionalSources.datasetTitle: Present and future Koppen-Geiger climate classification maps at 1-km resolution (2018)
additionalSources.org: Beck et al., Nature Scientific Data

climate.colorMeaning: Color encodes the Koppen-Geiger climate zone (e.g. tropical, arid, temperate, continental, polar).
climate.label: Koppen climate
climate.limitations: A rule-based discretization of continuous climate, so class boundaries are artificial and confidence is lower in data-sparse regions.
climate.methodology: Koppen-Geiger classes assigned at ~1 km resolution from topographically-corrected, observation-based temperature and precipitation climatologies.
climate.metric: Koppen-Geiger climate classification of each location based on temperature and precipitation regimes.

primarySource.datasetTitle: High-resolution (1 km) Koppen-Geiger maps, Version 2 (2023)
primarySource.org: Beck et al. (GloH2O), Nature Scientific Data

additionalSources.datasetTitle: EDGAR — Emissions Database for Global Atmospheric Research

co2pc.colorMeaning: Color encodes per-capita CO2 emissions, from low to high.
co2pc.label: CO2 per capita
co2pc.limitations: Production-based figures exclude trade-embodied (consumption) emissions and land-use change, understating the footprint of high-import economies.
co2pc.methodology: Territorial fossil-fuel and industry CO2 emissions estimated from energy and cement statistics, divided by population.
co2pc.metric: Territorial (production-based) fossil-fuel and industry CO2 emissions divided by population, tonnes per person per year.

primarySource.datasetTitle: Global Carbon Budget 2025

counterfeit.colorMeaning: Path color/weight encodes estimated provenance/transit volume of counterfeit goods.
counterfeit.label: Counterfeit goods
counterfeit.limitations: Based on seizures (biased toward well-enforced borders) with a multi-year lag, and provenance often shows transit hubs rather than true origin.
counterfeit.methodology: Provenance/transit corridors estimated from global customs seizure data (GTRIC index) combined with bilateral trade statistics.
counterfeit.metric: Estimated provenance and transit corridors of counterfeit and IP-infringing goods in world trade.

primarySource.datasetTitle: Mapping Global Trade in Fakes 2025

additionalSources.datasetTitle: Global Drifter Program surface current climatology

currents.colorMeaning: Lines/arrows encode current direction; color or weight may encode speed.
currents.label: Ocean currents
currents.limitations: OSCAR is a 0.25° model-derived product that smooths fine-scale and coastal features and represents only the surface mixed layer, not deep or instantaneous flow.
currents.methodology: OSCAR diagnoses near-surface currents from satellite sea-surface height, vector winds, and SST via a geostrophic/Ekman model; drifters measure currents directly.
currents.metric: Direction and speed of near-surface ocean currents.

primarySource.datasetTitle: OSCAR Surface Currents 0.25° Version 2.0

debtin.colorMeaning: Path color/weight encodes the amount each debtor country owes to creditor countries.
debtin.label: Bilateral debt (debtor side)
debtin.limitations: Coverage is debtor-reported and limited to LMIC borrowers; high-income borrowers are excluded and some creditor attribution is incomplete.
debtin.methodology: Compiles the external debt obligations of low- and middle-income borrowers reported via the Debtor Reporting System, broken out by creditor.
debtin.metric: Money owed: external debt that each low- and middle-income borrower owes to bilateral creditors.

primarySource.datasetTitle: International Debt Statistics (IDS) / International Debt Report 2025

debtout.colorMeaning: Path color/weight encodes the amount lent out from each creditor country to debtor countries.
debtout.label: Bilateral debt (creditor side)
debtout.limitations: Debtor-reported and limited to LMIC borrowers, so the creditor side is partial — lending among high-income countries and some non-Paris-Club/Chinese lending is inconsistently attributed.
debtout.methodology: Compiles external debt stocks and flows of low- and middle-income countries via the Debtor Reporting System, broken out by creditor type and increasingly by creditor country.
debtout.metric: Money lent out: external debt owed to each creditor country by low- and middle-income borrowers.

primarySource.datasetTitle: International Debt Statistics (IDS) / International Debt Report 2025

drugs.colorMeaning: Path color encodes drug type or trafficking corridor; weight is indicative of relative flow.
drugs.label: Drug routes
drugs.limitations: UNODC states routes are broadly indicative only; corridors are country-pair inferences drawn between centroids, not tracked geodata, and secondary routes may be missing.
drugs.methodology: Routes are inferred from seizure data and Member States' reported countries of departure, transit, and destination, aggregated into broadly indicative corridors.
drugs.metric: Indicative international trafficking corridors for illicit drugs.

primarySource.datasetTitle: World Drug Report 2025
primarySource.org: UN Office on Drugs and Crime

dust.colorMeaning: Path/shading encodes the direction and intensity of dust plume transport.
dust.label: Saharan dust
dust.limitations: No single 'dust route' dataset exists; this layer is synthesized from model and multi-sensor imagery, and plume paths are episodic and seasonal rather than fixed corridors.
dust.methodology: Dust transport modeled by the GEOS aerosol system assimilating MODIS AOD and other satellite data, with CALIPSO lidar providing vertical structure.
dust.metric: Seasonal/episodic atmospheric transport of Saharan mineral dust.

primarySource.datasetTitle: GEOS-FP aerosol product (dust AOT) with MODIS AOD and CALIPSO profiles

flights.colorMeaning: Lines depict airport-pair routes; weight may encode relative traffic.
flights.label: Flight corridors
flights.limitations: OpenFlights route data is frozen at June 2014 and is of historical value only; lines are great-circle approximations, not actual flown tracks (OAG/ICAO are paywalled).
flights.methodology: OpenFlights routes are straight-line airport-pair connections crowdsourced from a third-party feed; Eurocontrol derives flows from filed flight plans and radar tracks.
flights.metric: Scheduled air routes between airport pairs / air traffic corridors.

primarySource.datasetTitle: Airport, Airline and Route Database

flyways.colorMeaning: Color distinguishes the major flyway zones (color encodes category, not magnitude).
flyways.label: Bird migration flyways
flyways.limitations: Flyways are conceptual broad corridors and conservation constructs, not precise per-species paths; boundaries are smoothed and schematic.
flyways.methodology: Flyway boundaries are expert-delineated generalized zones synthesizing ringing/recovery, tracking, and species-distribution data.
flyways.metric: Generalized broad corridors used by migratory bird populations.

primarySource.datasetTitle: Global Flyways / DataZone migratory-bird profiles

food.colorMeaning: Path color/weight encodes the volume of food/grain traded along each corridor.
food.label: Food & grain trade
food.limitations: A one-to-two-year reporting lag and mirror-statistics discrepancies (reporter vs. partner figures often disagree).
food.methodology: Bilateral (reporter↔partner) import/export quantities and values by commodity, harmonized largely from UN Comtrade and national submissions.
food.metric: Bilateral import/export quantities and values of food and agricultural commodities.

primarySource.datasetTitle: FAOSTAT — Detailed trade matrix (crops and livestock products)

gdppc.colorMeaning: Color encodes GDP per capita, from lower to higher income.
gdppc.label: GDP per capita
gdppc.limitations: PPP conversion factors depend on periodic ICP price surveys and are extrapolated between benchmark years, carrying meaningful estimation uncertainty.
gdppc.methodology: GDP divided by mid-year population, converted at purchasing-power-parity factors from the International Comparison Program to equalize price levels.
gdppc.metric: Gross domestic product divided by mid-year population, in purchasing-power-parity international dollars.

primarySource.datasetTitle: World Development Indicators — GDP per capita, PPP (NY.GDP.PCAP.PP.CD)

govdebt.colorMeaning: Color encodes the gross government debt-to-GDP ratio, from low to high.
govdebt.label: Government debt (% of GDP)
govdebt.limitations: General-government coverage and gross-vs-net treatment differ across countries, and out-year figures are projections subject to large revision.
govdebt.methodology: Total gross debt liabilities of the general government sector as a share of GDP, compiled from country authorities and harmonized to a common framework.
govdebt.metric: General government gross debt as a share of GDP.

primarySource.datasetTitle: World Economic Outlook Database — General government gross debt, % of GDP (GGXWDG_NGDP)

govtype.colorMeaning: Color encodes the structural government-type category assigned to each country.
govtype.label: Government type
govtype.limitations: Now frozen and unmaintained as of Feb 2026; labels are descriptive and non-standardized rather than a coded academic typology.
govtype.methodology: Editorial classification by CIA analysts assigning each entity a descriptive label for its system of government.
govtype.metric: Descriptive classification of each country's system of government (e.g. federal presidential republic, parliamentary constitutional monarchy).

primarySource.datasetTitle: The World Factbook — Government type field

govtype.updateFrequency: static/historical (CIA discontinued the Factbook on 4 Feb 2026)

hdi.colorMeaning: Color encodes HDI from lower to higher human development.
hdi.label: Human Development Index
hdi.limitations: A national average that masks within-country inequality; the income dimension is capped, and a few countries lack a reported value (shown as no data).
hdi.methodology: Geometric mean of normalized indices for the three HDI dimensions (a long and healthy life, knowledge, and a decent standard of living).
hdi.metric: A composite of life expectancy at birth, education (mean and expected years of schooling), and gross national income per capita.

primarySource.datasetTitle: Human Development Report 2023/24 — Human Development Index (2022 values)

additionalSources.datasetTitle: WDI — Current health expenditure (% of GDP) (SH.XPD.CHEX.GD.ZS)

healthspend.colorMeaning: Color encodes total health spending as a share of GDP, from low to high.
healthspend.label: Health spending (% GDP)
healthspend.limitations: Cross-country comparability is limited by differing accounting practices, and donor flows are hard to capture in low-income countries.
healthspend.methodology: Sums all current health spending as a share of GDP under the System of Health Accounts (SHA 2011) framework.
healthspend.metric: Current health expenditure (public, private, and external) as a share of GDP.

primarySource.datasetTitle: Global Health Expenditure Database — Current health expenditure as % of GDP

hiv.colorMeaning: Color encodes adult HIV prevalence, from low to high.
hiv.label: HIV prevalence
hiv.limitations: Estimates carry wide uncertainty bounds, especially in concentrated epidemics where surveillance among key populations is incomplete.
hiv.methodology: Share of adults aged 15–49 living with HIV, modeled with the Spectrum/EPP tools using surveillance, survey, and programme data.
hiv.metric: Share of the population aged 15–49 living with HIV.

primarySource.datasetTitle: UNAIDS 2025 epidemiological estimates / AIDSinfo

internet.colorMeaning: Color encodes the percentage of the population online, from low to high.
internet.label: Internet use
internet.limitations: Definitions of 'Internet use' and survey recency vary by country, so many developing-country figures are ITU estimates rather than directly measured.
internet.methodology: Compiled from national household surveys and administrative data reported to ITU, with modelling to fill gaps and produce comparable global figures.
internet.metric: Share of individuals using the Internet as a percentage of population.

primarySource.datasetTitle: Measuring Digital Development: Facts and Figures 2025

additionalSources.datasetTitle: Ethnologue: Languages of the World, 28th edition

language.colorMeaning: Color encodes the language family of the country's dominant or official language.
language.label: Language family
language.limitations: Language-vs-dialect splitting decisions are contested among linguists, and a single 'dominant language per country' obscures multilingual states.
language.methodology: Glottolog provides a rigorously curated genealogical classification of the world's languages keyed to Glottocodes; dominant language per country is assigned editorially.
language.metric: Dominant language and its genealogical language family for each country.

primarySource.datasetTitle: Glottolog 5.3
primarySource.org: Max Planck Institute for Evolutionary Anthropology

additionalSources.datasetTitle: Criminalisation maps / sexual orientation laws maps

lgbt.colorMeaning: Color encodes the level of legal protection vs. criminalization for LGBTQ+ people.
lgbt.label: LGBTQ+ legal status
lgbt.limitations: Captures laws on the books rather than enforcement or lived reality, and snapshots lag real-time legal change between editions.
lgbt.methodology: Surveys laws across 193 UN member states in multiple legal categories (criminalization, anti-discrimination, recognition, marriage, gender recognition).
lgbt.metric: Legal status of LGBTQ+ people, from criminalization of same-sex acts through anti-discrimination protections and marriage equality.

primarySource.datasetTitle: Laws on Us: A Global Overview of Legal Progress and Backtracking on SOGIESC

lgbt.updateFrequency: periodic (report); maps updated as laws change

lifeexp.colorMeaning: Color encodes life expectancy at birth, from lower to higher.
lifeexp.label: Life expectancy
lifeexp.limitations: Assumes today's mortality stays fixed, so it does not predict any actual person's lifespan, and figures lag real time by about two years.
lifeexp.methodology: Period (synthetic-cohort) life expectancy compiled from UN World Population Prospects and national statistical offices.
lifeexp.metric: Number of years a newborn would live if current mortality patterns held constant throughout life.

primarySource.datasetTitle: World Development Indicators — Life expectancy at birth, total (SP.DYN.LE00.IN)

matmort.colorMeaning: Color encodes the maternal mortality ratio, from low to high.
matmort.label: Maternal mortality
matmort.limitations: Maternal deaths are frequently misclassified or underreported, so most country figures are modeled with broad uncertainty ranges.
matmort.methodology: Maternal deaths per 100,000 live births estimated with a Bayesian model combining vital registration, surveys, and censuses.

primarySource.datasetTitle: Trends in Maternal Mortality 2000 to 2023
primarySource.org: UN Maternal Mortality Estimation Inter-Agency Group (WHO, UNICEF, UNFPA, World Bank, UN DESA)

migration.colorMeaning: Path color/weight encodes the size of the migrant stock along each origin–destination corridor.
migration.label: Migration corridors
migration.limitations: A stock snapshot of where migrants live, not a flow, so drawing origin–destination as a moving path is an interpolation; the World Bank bilateral matrix ends at 2000.
migration.methodology: Estimates foreign-born persons residing in each country by origin and destination, built mainly from population censuses and registers.
migration.metric: Origin-to-destination stock of international migrants (foreign-born persons residing in each country).

primarySource.datasetTitle: International Migrant Stock 2024

minerals.colorMeaning: Path color/weight encodes the volume of minerals/metals traded or sourced along each corridor.
minerals.label: Minerals & metals trade
minerals.limitations: US-centric — gives global production and US import sources, not full bilateral world flow matrices; country-to-country flows require UN Comtrade.
minerals.methodology: Reports per-commodity world production and reserves plus US net import reliance and major source countries.
minerals.metric: World production, reserves, and trade/source flows of mineral commodities and metals.

primarySource.datasetTitle: Mineral Commodity Summaries 2026

oil.colorMeaning: Path color/weight encodes the volume of oil/gas traded along each corridor.
oil.label: Oil & gas trade
oil.limitations: Trade-movement tables are inter-regional aggregates, not country-to-country pipeline/tanker geometry; granular bilateral flows require UN Comtrade or IEA.
oil.methodology: Compiles national/industry production, consumption, and inter-regional trade-movement matrices (origin region → destination region).
oil.metric: Inter-regional and bilateral trade movements of crude oil, refined products, and natural gas.

primarySource.datasetTitle: Statistical Review of World Energy 2025 (74th edition)

physicians.colorMeaning: Color encodes physician density, from low to high.
physicians.label: Physicians per 1,000
physicians.limitations: Country data years differ widely (latest-available is used), and figures count registered/licensed doctors rather than those actively practicing.
physicians.methodology: Counts generalist and specialist medical practitioners per population, reported by national authorities via the NHWA platform.
physicians.metric: Number of generalist and specialist medical doctors per 1,000 population.

primarySource.datasetTitle: Global Health Workforce Statistics / National Health Workforce Accounts — Medical doctors

popdensity.colorMeaning: Color encodes population density, from sparse to dense.
popdensity.label: Population density
popdensity.limitations: A national average that masks enormous internal variation (deserts vs. cities) and is sensitive to how land area is defined.
popdensity.methodology: Mid-year total population (UN WPP) divided by land area in square kilometers (FAO), excluding inland water bodies.
popdensity.metric: Mid-year population divided by land area, people per square kilometer.

primarySource.datasetTitle: World Development Indicators — Population density (EN.POP.DNST)

refugees.colorMeaning: Path color/weight encodes the size of the refugee population along each origin–asylum corridor.
refugees.label: Refugee flows
refugees.limitations: Reflects registered/recognized populations residing in host countries (an origin–asylum pairing), not real-time crossing flows; unregistered populations are undercounted.
refugees.methodology: Compiles refugee, asylum-seeker, IDP, and stateless populations by origin and asylum country from government and UNHCR registration/reporting.
refugees.metric: Refugee and asylum-seeker populations by country of origin and country of asylum.

primarySource.datasetTitle: Refugee Data Finder (Population Statistics Database)

regime.colorMeaning: Color encodes regime category, typically from more democratic to more autocratic.
regime.label: Regime type
regime.limitations: Relies on subjective expert judgments aggregated via measurement models, introducing rater uncertainty; Polity5 is frozen at 2018 and should not be treated as current.
regime.methodology: V-Dem aggregates thousands of expert codings across hundreds of indicators into democracy indices and a Regimes-of-the-World typology.
regime.metric: Classification of each country along the democracy–autocracy spectrum (e.g. liberal democracy, electoral democracy, electoral autocracy, closed autocracy).

primarySource.datasetTitle: V-Dem Dataset v16 / Democracy Report 2026

additionalSources.org: Association of Religion Data Archives (ARDA) / World Religion Database

religion.colorMeaning: Color encodes the dominant or plurality religious group in each country.
religion.label: Religion by branch
religion.limitations: Resolves only seven broad categories, not denominational branches (e.g. Sunni/Shia, Catholic/Protestant), and self-identification quality varies widely by country.
religion.methodology: Religious composition estimated for seven broad categories from more than 2,700 sources including national censuses, demographic surveys, and population registers.
religion.metric: Share of each country's population identifying with major religious groups (Christian, Muslim, Hindu, Buddhist, Jewish, other, unaffiliated).

primarySource.datasetTitle: How the Global Religious Landscape Changed from 2010 to 2020

remittances.colorMeaning: Path color/weight encodes the estimated value of remittances along each corridor.
remittances.label: Remittance corridors
remittances.limitations: The bilateral corridor cells are modeled, not measured — only country-level totals are real, and informal/unrecorded transfers are excluded.
remittances.methodology: Allocates each country's measured total remittance inflows across source countries in proportion to migrant stocks and per-capita incomes of host vs. origin.
remittances.metric: Estimated bilateral remittance transfers from host countries to origin countries.

primarySource.datasetTitle: Bilateral Remittance Matrix

sanitation.colorMeaning: Color encodes access to safely managed sanitation, from low to high.
sanitation.label: Sanitation access
sanitation.limitations: Data on the final disposal or treatment of excreta are sparse in many countries, so safely managed estimates are modeled and often unavailable nationally.
sanitation.methodology: Share of population using an improved, non-shared facility where excreta are safely disposed in situ or transported and treated offsite.
sanitation.metric: Share of population using safely managed sanitation services (improved, non-shared facility with safe disposal or treatment of excreta).

primarySource.datasetTitle: Progress on Household Drinking Water, Sanitation and Hygiene 2000–2024

shipping.colorMeaning: Path color/weight encodes maritime traffic density or transit volume.
shipping.label: Shipping lanes
shipping.limitations: AIS is subject to jamming, spoofing, and vessels going dark, and downloadable density layers are derived estimates, not raw tracks (MarineTraffic is commercial).
shipping.methodology: PortWatch estimates trade flows from satellite AIS signals on ~90,000 ships processed with big-data/ML models; UNCTAD aggregates national seaborne-trade statistics.
shipping.metric: Maritime traffic density along major shipping lanes and through chokepoints.

primarySource.datasetTitle: PortWatch (Ports & Chokepoints datasets)

silkroad.colorMeaning: Lines depict reconstructed historical trade routes (color distinguishes branches, not magnitude).
silkroad.label: Silk Road
silkroad.limitations: Interpretive historical corridors that are approximate, contested, and stylized; UNESCO's authoritative route geometry (Interactive Atlas) is still in development.
silkroad.methodology: Routes are scholarly reconstructions of historical exchange networks compiled by UNESCO and partner historians.
silkroad.metric: Reconstructed historical routes of the Silk Road exchange networks.

primarySource.datasetTitle: Silk Roads Programme — Interactive Map / Online Platform

additionalSources.datasetTitle: International Migration Outlook / Education at a Glance

students.colorMeaning: Path color/weight encodes the number of mobile students along each origin–destination corridor.
students.label: International students
students.limitations: Origin detail is incomplete (often only by region for inbound), and definitions of 'mobile' vary by country, so some corridors are partial.
students.methodology: Counts tertiary students enrolled outside their country of origin, by destination and origin region/country, reported by national authorities.
students.metric: Tertiary students enrolled outside their country of origin, by origin and destination.

primarySource.datasetTitle: Inbound/Outbound Internationally Mobile Students

trade.colorMeaning: Path color/weight encodes the value of merchandise trade along each bilateral corridor.
trade.label: Trade flows
trade.limitations: Reporting lags and gaps leave some recent partners incomplete, and importer- vs. exporter-reported figures for the same corridor often differ (mirror asymmetry).
trade.methodology: Compiles official bilateral import/export merchandise statistics reported by national statistical authorities, by partner and commodity.

primarySource.datasetTitle: UN Comtrade Database

trafficking.colorMeaning: Path color/weight encodes the origin–destination flow of detected trafficking victims.
trafficking.label: Human trafficking
trafficking.limitations: Reflects only detected victims and is heavily shaped by national detection capacity, so flows show where victims are found, not true scale or all routes.
trafficking.methodology: Cross-border flows derived from detected-victim citizenship vs. country of detection, aggregated into origin–destination region pairs.
trafficking.metric: Cross-border origin-to-destination flows of detected trafficking victims.

primarySource.datasetTitle: Global Report on Trafficking in Persons 2024
primarySource.org: UN Office on Drugs and Crime

additionalSources.datasetTitle: Levels and Trends in Child Mortality

under5mort.colorMeaning: Color encodes the under-5 mortality rate, from low to high.
under5mort.label: Under-5 mortality
under5mort.limitations: For countries lacking strong vital registration, estimates rely on modeled survey data with wide uncertainty intervals.
under5mort.methodology: Estimated via a Bayesian B-spline model fitting surveys, censuses, and vital registration data.
under5mort.metric: Probability per 1,000 live births that a child dies before reaching age five.

primarySource.datasetTitle: Levels & Trends in Child Mortality: Report 2024
primarySource.org: UN Inter-agency Group for Child Mortality Estimation (UNICEF, WHO, World Bank, UN DESA)

voyages.colorMeaning: Lines depict reconstructed historical voyage routes (color distinguishes era/trade, not magnitude).
voyages.label: Age of Exploration
voyages.limitations: Routes are point-to-point reconstructions from incomplete records (not actual sailed tracks); Age-of-Exploration explorer routes have no canonical open dataset and must be curated separately.
voyages.methodology: Each voyage is reconstructed from archival shipping and customs records, with routes inferred from documented embarkation and disembarkation points.
voyages.metric: Reconstructed maritime routes of Age-of-Exploration and transatlantic slave-trade voyages.

primarySource.datasetTitle: Trans-Atlantic Slave Trade Database

water.colorMeaning: Color encodes access to safely managed drinking water, from low to high.
water.label: Safe drinking water
water.limitations: Many countries lack water-quality and accessibility data, so the 'safely managed' tier must be estimated and is unavailable for a substantial share of the population.
water.methodology: Share of population using an improved water source on premises, available when needed and free of contamination, modeled from surveys, censuses, and administrative data.
water.metric: Share of population using safely managed drinking water services (improved source, on premises, available when needed, free of contamination).

primarySource.datasetTitle: Progress on Household Drinking Water, Sanitation and Hygiene 2000–2024

wildlife.colorMeaning: Path color/weight encodes indicative wildlife trafficking corridors between source and destination regions.
wildlife.label: Wildlife trafficking
wildlife.limitations: Seizure-based, so it maps interdiction points and reporting effort; successful (un-seized) flows and non-reporting countries are invisible.
wildlife.methodology: Trafficking patterns built from national annual illegal-trade (seizure) reports submitted by CITES Parties.
wildlife.metric: Indicative trafficking corridors for illegally traded wildlife and wildlife products.

primarySource.datasetTitle: World Wildlife Crime Report 2024
primarySource.org: UN Office on Drugs and Crime (for the CITES Secretariat)

wood.colorMeaning: Path color/weight encodes the volume of timber/wood traded along each corridor.
wood.label: Timber & wood trade
wood.limitations: Headline domain is production plus aggregate trade by country, not full bilateral matrices, and excludes illegal/unrecorded logging; partner-level flows need the trade matrix or Comtrade.
wood.methodology: Annual production and trade quantities/values for wood and paper products, collected via the joint FAO/ITTO/Eurostat/UNECE questionnaire.
wood.metric: Production and trade quantities/values of wood and paper products (roundwood, sawnwood, panels, pulp, paper).

primarySource.datasetTitle: FAOSTAT — Forestry Production and Trade
